correctness.rationale: Exact zero-sum decomposition separates a strictly negative core-fluctuation sector, an antisymmetric 2x2 sector positive for p<2, and a symmetric 2x2 sector with determinant -k[kU(p)+V(p)]. Monotonic derivatives prove a unique threshold (1,2), and an explicit kernel vector has sum zero. Li–Weston exponent reduction excludes higher exponents. Euclidean ranks are centered-Gram ranks; the separately constructed adjacency-derived checker corroborates 528 rational identities and finite signatures but does not replace proof.

originality.rationale: A sharp all-orders scalar equation, complete endpoint equality vector, strict clique-size monotonicity and first-order large-size limit are established for bull-type graphs with leaves at distinct clique vertices. The inspected general negative-type works provide criteria and interval results, not these evaluated quantities. Related one-attachment bouquets and two-clique sums are nonisomorphic and their exact formulas do not imply this one. Literature and indexed-record coverage is incomplete; priority is not certified.
residual_risks: No claim of exhaustive coverage of all literature or full source archives: an equivalent all-order formula could be unindexed.

value.rationale: The family is the minimal two-distinct-attachment extension of a clique (a bull-graph clique expansion), and its 3-distance geometry is not captured by one-hub clique bouquets. The theorem gives a nontrivial exact exponent for every clique order, a complete critical equality classification, the dimension drop, strict size monotonicity and a computable limiting exponent with an inverse-order correction, each tied to the natural parameter of core redundancy.
